annotation.title_clean: Resolution on the need to undertake a Study on human and peoples' rights and artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and other new and emerging technologies in Africa - ACHPR/Res. 473 (EXT.OS/ XXXI) 2021
annotation.title_en: Resolution on the need to undertake a Study on human and peoples' rights and artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and other new and emerging technologies in Africa - ACHPR/Res. 473 (EXT.OS/ XXXI) 2021
annotation.authors_or_issuer: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (ACHPR)
named_instruments_referenced: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
ACHPR General Comment No. 3 on Article 4
AU Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy for Africa
annotation.summary_en: ACHPR Resolution 473 (2021), adopted at its 31st Extraordinary Session, calls for a study of how AI, robotics and emerging technologies affect human and peoples' rights in Africa. It notes there is no comprehensive governance framework, raises privacy, discrimination and disinformation concerns, and calls for meaningful human control over autonomous systems, including autonomous weapons.
key_provisions_or_claims: Commissions a study on AI, robotics and emerging technologies and human and peoples' rights in Africa
Notes the absence of a comprehensive framework ensuring that AI companies comply with human rights obligations
Reaffirms that machine autonomy in selecting human targets or using force must be subject to meaningful human control
Highlights risks to privacy, equality, non-discrimination, expression and socio-economic rights
Calls for African participation in international AI governance frameworks
